description: Observed-order-of-accuracy sweep for the sixth-order inhomogeneous-Dirichlet rule central_D2_6_dirichlet_bc driven by problems/heat_1d_dirichlet_o6.esm. The problem file is loaded once per resolution with the loader-API metaparameter binding of N (esm-spec 9.7.6 binding site 4) — no per-resolution fixture files. The manufactured solution exp(-alpha pi^2 t) sin(pi x) + gL + (gR - gL) x is exact for the continuous PDE with constant wall values gL = 0.5, gR = 1.5 (derivation in the problem file); the steady linear profile is discretely exact (all interior and boundary closure weight-sums are zero), so the recorded L2/Linf errors at t=0.1 are pure spatial-discretization error from the sine mode. Both the interior 7-point stencil and the one-sided boundary-row closures are derived to be O(dx^6) (each closure exact for polynomials up to degree 7, verified symbolically), so the ASYMPTOTIC design order is 6 and expected_order is pinned to that design order. HONEST OBSERVED BEHAVIOR: the Julia sweep over n=8..64 gives median pairwise orders 6.22 (L2, pairwise 7.22/6.22/5.52) and 5.99 (Linf, pairwise 7.56/5.99/3.90). The coarse end is pre-asymptotically SUPERCONVERGENT (at n=8 six of the eight cells are boundary-closure rows, so the 8->16 ratio runs to ~7.2-7.6); the finest 32->64 ratio softens (5.52 L2, 3.90 Linf) because the tiny O(h^6) error there (~1e-13) dips below the 1e-12 integrator tolerance floor. The check's median-of-pairwise rejects both the coarse-superconvergent and the fine near-floor extreme and lands on the true sixth order; nothing is fudged. The 7-point interior stencil and the seven-cell boundary closures require N >= 7, so the sweep starts at N = 8. order_tolerance is widened to 0.6 (vs the 0.2 used for the clean fourth-order Dirichlet sibling, one order up with a stronger pre-asymptotic transient) so the 6.0 design order brackets the observed 5.99-6.22 median spread. Integrator tolerances are tightened to 1e-12/1e-14 so the errors stay spatial-dominated; the golden comparison atol 1e-9 keeps the near-floor finest row cross-binding reproducible (all bindings agree the error is ~0 within 1e-9).
